title: kv-cache: adaptive memory manager and eviction policy for fragmentation / paging / spillover
author: Ava Thompson
description: Motivation: production KV cache in the serving runtime experiences space fragmentation and unpredictable paging/spillover under mixed-length workloads, which increases latency tail and costs. This PR implements an adaptive KV cache memory manager with defect/fragmentation-aware eviction, smart paging thresholds, and controlled spillover to persistent store. Design: 1) compacting allocator to reduce internal fragmentation by coalescing free segments during low-load windows; 2) eviction scoring that combines LRU recency, segment fragmentation metric, and estimated rehydration cost to prefer evicting high-fragmentation/low-value segments; 3) paging policy that triggers proactive page-out based on predicted working set and per-model QoS targets; 4) spillover queue with rate-limited background flush to object store and prioritized prefetch on warmup; 5) fast-path behavioral knobs exposed via runtime config (kv.compaction_interval_ms, kv.eviction_bias_fragmentation, kv.paging_threshold_pct, kv.spillover_rate_limit). Implementation: allocator and eviction implemented in runtime/kv_cache.cpp and include/kv_cache.h, added eviction scheduler hooks in scheduler/scheduler.cpp, metrics and tracing in observability/kv_metrics.{h,cpp}, unit and integration tests under tests/kv_eviction_test.cpp and perf/bench_kv_spillover.py. Backwards compatibility: default behavior preserves previous eviction decisions when knobs are unset. Rollout plan: staged rollout using feature flag "kv-adaptive-memory-manager" with 10% -> 50% -> 100% canary windows, observe kv.fragmentation_ratio, p50/p95 tail latency for short/long sequences, and backend spillover bytes/sec. Benchmarks: microbench on A100 (seq=256/2048) shows 18% p95 tail reduction for long sequences and 12% lower average GPU memory pressure vs baseline. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests - [x] perf benchmarks - [x] feature flag + rollout plan Related: ENG-2481 (KV memory manager design), ENG-2513 (spillover prefetch), SUP-4123 (customer incident caused by aggressive paging).

discussion: Diego Marquez (reviewer): Can you justify the compaction interval default? It looks aggressive for high-throughput workloads.
Ava Thompson (author): Default is 30s; microbench showed compaction at 30s reduces fragmentation by ~40% while keeping CPU overhead <2%. We expose kv.compaction_interval_ms for tuning.
Priya Patel (reviewer): Eviction score mixes three signals - did you calibrate weights across different models?

Ava Thompson: Yes, we calibrated on a mixed production trace (chat + long-doc). The default eviction_bias_fragmentation=0.6 favors compacting segments to free contiguous memory when fragmentation explains >20% of free space.
Evan Liu (reviewer): Found a race in compaction worker causing a double-free in low-memory simulated tests.
Ava Thompson: Fixed in commit 'Fix race in compaction worker' by switching to epoch-based reclamation and adding unit test that reproduces the race.
Priya Patel: CI failed on first run due to flaky test in bench harness. Please stabilize before merge.
Ava Thompson: Addressed by adding retry/backoff in bench harness and marking the synthetic load as stable. Rerun CI - all green.
Diego Marquez: Approved after confirming metrics instrumentation and rollout plan.
release_notes: Adaptive KV cache memory manager: reduces fragmentation, improves eviction decisions, adds controlled spillover to object store, new runtime knobs for compaction and paging. Metrics exposed: kv.fragmentation_ratio, kv.evicted_bytes, kv.spillover_rate.
notes: This PR is primarily in runtime with small scheduler and observability changes. Monitored with canary feature flag. No user-facing API changes.
